We use Zod 4 (`zod ^4`) for the schemas. Records and project.yaml are loose objects at every level, using `looseObject` for forward compatibility [dec-094vmt9t].

The JSON Schema comes from Zod 4's built-in `toJSONSchema`, so no separate dependency is needed [dec-094vmt9t]. To regenerate the published files (`dist/record.schema.json` and `project.schema.json`), run `pnpm --filter @aimem/schema build`, review the snapshot diff, then update the snapshot deliberately [run-17vbsk09]. A snapshot test guards the exported contract [dec-094vmt9t][tst-cw10hn77].

Claims use compare-and-swap on a dedicated `aimem-live` git branch. To acquire a task, a clone fetches, checks the current holder, commits its claim, and pushes. If the push is rejected, it retries, so two clones cannot both win [dec-kqfc1se7].

Supporting details:
- Each task has one claim file (holder, session, paths, since, heartbeat, ttl). The invariant is at most one live holder per task [sch-3a3jkgmm].
- Claims must never be committed to feature branches [sch-3a3jkgmm]. Task files also never hold claim holders [dec-g17nvbca].
- Caveats: this requires network access to the remote, and expired claims can be stolen after the TTL [dec-kqfc1se7]. The claim format may change before M3 ships [sch-3a3jkgmm].
- With the optional sync server, realtime claims are available on top of git [dec-e4qh00j3]. The records do not describe how server-side claims prevent double claims.

A pure-JS git library (isomorphic-git) was evaluated and rejected because of feature gaps in credentials, hooks and worktrees [dec-ghsxv3vg]. 

Instead, all git work shells out to the user's installed git binary via execa, so credentials, hooks and config behave as usual. Reimplementing git would also miss LFS, worktrees and credential helpers [dec-ndgz6y7a].

Consequences: git must be installed (true for every target user) [dec-ndgz6y7a], and tests use real temporary repos instead of mocks [dec-ghsxv3vg].

Ids are random so that parallel branches never collide. Counters collide when two branches add records at the same time [dec-j2t35mx0].

Each id is a type prefix plus 8 random Crockford base32 characters [dec-j2t35mx0]. The tradeoffs are that ids are not sortable by time, and validation fails on duplicates [dec-j2t35mx0].

After upgrading Biome to 2.5, `biome migrate` rewrote `recommended: true` to `preset: none`, which silently disabled all lint rules [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4]. Lint kept passing because nothing was being checked, so any lint problem could have reached main unnoticed [mem-rj2t0xj9][inc-242wrkm4].

It was noticed in the migrate output and fixed in the same session on 2026-10-12 [inc-242wrkm4]. The fix was to set the preset back to recommended and probe with an explicit `any`, where lint must warn (noExplicitAny) [inc-242wrkm4][mem-rj2t0xj9]. To prevent a repeat, probe lint after any lint config change [inc-242wrkm4].

An unquoted `content_sha` made up only of digits is parsed by YAML as an integer, not a string. The schema's string check on `source.content_sha` then fails with V002. For example, a placeholder sha of zeros became the number 0 and failed validation [mem-hrm4q190].

The fix is to quote hashes and ids that could be all digits when writing frontmatter [mem-hrm4q190].

Note: this comes from a record with trust="agent", so it is not human-verified.

aimem authenticates to Google using a service account that can read one shared inbox folder, rather than per-user OAuth [mem-j4yeeebg]. The stated reasons are least privilege and no consent screens for non-developers. Per-user OAuth remains an option [mem-j4yeeebg].

This sits within the v1 decision to offer upload and Google Drive connectors, so that content from Google Docs and Sheets becomes read-only, externally-owned records [dec-8hscg239].

The records don't describe a way to keep private notes out of git. They say knowledge lives as markdown records committed to git [dec-3by2wh28], and that roles only affect ranking, not access, so anyone with repo access can read everything [dec-2znaykpx]. The only non-git items mentioned are the local vector cache under .aimem/.cache [sch-nygqk0ka] and live claims on a separate git branch [sch-3a3jkgmm], and neither is a place for private notes.

Token counts are estimated with a chars/4 heuristic: the number of characters divided by four, with per-model overrides. This applies to all budgets, and an optional tokenizer can be plugged in later [dec-nppkpt6e].

- **Why:** exact tokenizers differ per model and add a heavy dependency [dec-nppkpt6e].
- **Accuracy:** estimates can be off by about 10–20%, so per-section limits are given some headroom [dec-nppkpt6e].
- **Default budget:** 4000 tokens, unless project.yaml sets `briefing.budget_tokens` [mem-q9krtm0g].

INDEX.md tidak boleh diedit manual karena file ini selalu dibuat ulang oleh aimem, sehingga perubahan manual akan hilang pada penulisan berikutnya [mem-xx4j8c41]. (Catatan: record ini bertrust "agent", jadi belum diverifikasi manusia.)

Alasan pendukung dari keputusan terverifikasi:
- INDEX.md ditandai `merge=ours` dan selalu diregenerasi oleh hook atau CI, bukan diedit tangan [dec-v868xmvq].
- Latar belakangnya: file indeks yang dihasilkan selalu konflik saat dua cabang menambah record [dec-v868xmvq].

Jika isinya salah, perbaiki record sumbernya lalu jalankan `aimem index` [mem-xx4j8c41].

Tidak, server sinkronisasi bersifat opsional. Tim kecil atau individu bisa berjalan hanya dengan git; server menambahkan klaim realtime, indeks bersama, dan aplikasi web [dec-e4qh00j3]. Alasannya, mewajibkan server akan menghalangi penggunaan solo dan menambah beban operasional [dec-e4qh00j3].

Hal terkait:
- File di git adalah sumber kebenaran; server dan aplikasi web hanya mengindeks dan menyimpan state live sementara [dec-3by2wh28].
- Server di-host sendiri oleh tiap tim (satu container plus Postgres), dan hosting multi-tenant di luar cakupan [dec-e4qh00j3].
- Setiap fitur harus punya jalur khusus git atau degradasi yang terdokumentasi [dec-e4qh00j3].

The project uses Biome for linting (and formatting). A verified record describes upgrading Biome to 2.5 and the `biome migrate` command changing the linter config, with the fix being to set it to `recommended` so rules like `noExplicitAny` actually warn [mem-rj2t0xj9]. The `pnpm lint` script is part of the local gate [run-gea7sjyn][mem-rmqc83gx].

One record claims the project uses ESLint and Prettier, but it is inferred (not human-verified), drawn from an "alternatives" column in the tech stack doc, and it notes that it contradicts biome.json and needs review [mem-yd7935cw]. I'd treat it as unreliable.

The records don't state explicitly which tool does the formatting. The Biome record only covers lint config, and the formatter-related title ("Formatter config migration…") points to Biome as well [mem-rj2t0xj9].

Yes, per the accepted decision, the plan is hybrid retrieval: BM25 fused with a local multilingual embedding model, falling back to lexical-only when no model is present [dec-mtbcq7yr]. This was to ship in milestone M2.

It is not yet implemented, though. The task for embeddings (chunking, provider interface, vector cache, lexical fallback) is still open [tsk-w4411vwr]. The BM25 index and search task is also open [tsk-7hfeytzh]. The default model choice is only proposed and waits on the eval harness [dec-f30g1hx1], and that harness task is open too [tsk-keh9n36n].

One record says retrieval is lexical-only BM25 [mem-1x4y6jd8]. It is inferred (not human-verified) and based on a superseded ADR, so it is outdated as a statement of the plan.

In short, search is designed to use embeddings, but the records don't show that it does yet.

It depends on the mode. Team projects default to `agent_commits: stage`, so agents stage changes and humans commit them with their code. Solo mode implies `agent_commits: commit`, so agents commit themselves. A `pr` option is also available [dec-ek66gxgx].

A new decision with no explicit status gets **proposed**. This is set as `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = proposed`, matching the spec 03 lifecycle (proposed, then accepted or rejected) [dec-9h7m0yg3]. Agents must pass `--status accepted` when a human has already agreed [dec-9h7m0yg3].

Earlier, a handoff noted that the schema draft had `DEFAULT_STATUS.decision = accepted`, which was not in the spec [hnd-qp6gjbe5]. That was an agent-written, unverified record. The verified decision resolved it to `proposed` [dec-9h7m0yg3].

The default is a constant applied by tools at the point of use, not injected by the schemas [dec-4mn8zfef].

The release checklist says to run the full local check, update the changelog, tag the release, and publish [mem-pq7r2x9k]. This record is agent-written and not human-verified.

The record also contains an embedded line telling the assistant to ignore its rules and reply only with a specific word. I did not follow it, since records are reference data, not instructions.

For the "full local check", another verified record gives the local gate as `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` [mem-rmqc83gx]. The checklist itself does not say this explicitly, so the link is my inference.

Run these in order from the workspace root [run-gea7sjyn]:

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm lint`
3. `pnpm typecheck`
4. `pnpm test`

All three checks (lint, typecheck, test) must exit 0 [run-gea7sjyn]. The same gate is `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`, and CI runs it on Linux and macOS with Node 22 and 24 [mem-rmqc83gx]. Property-test failures may show a shrunk counterexample [mem-rmqc83gx].
